organizations.name: Climate Action Against Disinformation (CAAD)
organizations.role: Coalition of climate and anti-disinformation organisations that monitors and documents climate disinformation trends across platforms.
organizations.framing_note: Frame claims the way CAAD does: name the tactic, document the pattern, cite the evidence. Avoid overstating certainty.

publications.title: CAAD reports and briefings on climate disinformation

organizations.name: GreenLatinos
organizations.role: National Latine environmental organisation. Its Climate Conexiones programme works specifically on Spanish-language climate disinformation.
organizations.framing_note: Centre Latine communities as knowledgeable actors, never as passive victims. The organisation's own framing is 'Luchando por la Liberacion Ambiental'.

publications.title: Rumores Renovables: report exposing a global Spanish-language climate disinformation network
Climate Loteria - bilingual myth-busting card campaign

organizations.name: Friends of the Earth
organizations.role: Research, with Roots and Purpose, on disinformation that escalates during extreme weather events in Latin America.
organizations.framing_note: Emphasise that non-English disinformation is more prevalent and less moderated than English-language disinformation.

publications.title: Report: extreme weather disinformation in Latin America

organizations.name: Climate Power En Accion
organizations.role: Spanish-language climate communications programme focused on clean energy, jobs and community benefits.
organizations.framing_note: Lead with jobs, health and family benefits that are concrete and local rather than abstract climate targets.

publications.title: Climate Power En Accion - research and messaging resources

organizations.name: Resource Media / Grow Progress message test
organizations.role: Ran the 2025 randomised message test with GreenLatinos on 1,797 Latinx adults that produced the measured value-frame data this project routes on.
organizations.framing_note: The measured lifts in frames.json come from this study. Treat them as the ground truth for framing decisions.

publications.title: GreenLatinos Grow Progress Message Test Report (2025)

reporting_channels.how: Hold the message, tap Report, and choose the reason. Forwarding it onward is what spreads it - screenshot instead when you want to ask someone about it.
reporting_channels.note: WhatsApp is end-to-end encrypted, so moderation happens at the account level rather than the message level.

reporting_channels.how: Use the three-dot menu on the post, then Report, then False information.
reporting_channels.note: Spanish-language fact-checking coverage is thinner than English; reporting still matters.

reporting_channels.how: Three dots under the video, Report, Misinformation.
